bullets.title: Broadcom AVGO post-earnings down on soft AI guidance despite strong beat
bullets.body: AVGO reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $22.19B (+48% YoY), beating estimates, with AI semiconductor bookings exceeding $30B vs. $10.8B shipped. However, Q3 AI semiconductor guidance of $16B came in slightly below the elevated market expectation near $17.2B, sending shares down 6-7% AH. Multiple desks note investors had expected a raise to the $100B+ 2027 revenue target rather than a reiteration. 'Revenue range remains intact' per analyst commentary.

bullets.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang calls Marvell 'next trillion-dollar company' at Computex; MRVL surges 30%+
bullets.body: Jensen Huang called Marvell a potential trillion-dollar company on stage at Computex Taiwan, citing its role in AI data center connectivity. MRVL shares surged 20-33% on the commentary; current market cap is ~$191B, implying ~5x upside to $1T. JPM and Northland also raised price targets on MRVL. Supply chain checks show Marvell winning the Google TPUv9 networking chip (Teralynx T100, 102.4 Tbps) to be manufactured on Intel's 18A process with mass production targeted by end-2027.

bullets.title: Google (Alphabet) raises $80B for AI capex; Berkshire commits $10B
bullets.body: Alphabet announced an $80B equity raise split across: $40B ATM offering, $30B underwritten offerings, and a $10B strategic investment from Berkshire Hathaway. The equity raise is being used to accelerate AI infrastructure. GOOGL stock fell ~2-3% in after-hours on dilution concerns, though analysts note the $80B is only ~1.8% of its $4.5T market cap. Goldman models imply 2027 CapEx will increase 'significantly' vs. the $190B 2026 guide.

bullets.title: Nvidia Vera Rubin enters full production; Computex reveals full agentic AI stack
bullets.body: Nvidia announced Vera Rubin NVL72 is now in full production, with Foxconn manufacturing trays at one per minute on fully automated lines. Jensen also announced the Vera CPU—projected to generate >$20B in standalone revenue—and unveiled the full AI factory stack including RTX Spark for PCs, a partnership with Microsoft, and Cosmos 3 for physical AI. NVDA shares gained 6.3% on the session, adding $319B in market cap. Jensen simultaneously named Marvell as the 'next trillion-dollar company.'

bullets.title: Micron (MU) options volume exceeds SPY + QQQ combined; monthly RSI above 90
bullets.body: MU options traded ~$1.5B in premium in a single session—more than SPY and QQQ combined—while the stock reached a market cap above $1T, representing a 10x+ gain over the prior year. Monthly RSI crossed above 90, levels not seen in 30+ years. Multiple JOLTS and manufacturing data beats were cited as macro tailwinds, but Barclays raised concerns about the AI rally becoming 'increasingly vulnerable.' Nvidia confirmed all three major HBM4 suppliers (MU, Samsung, SK Hynix) are now qualified.

bullets.title: HPE surges 30%+ on AI-driven earnings beat and dramatically raised FY2026 guidance
bullets.body: HPE reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $10.68B vs. $9.79B estimate (9% beat), with full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised to $3.35-$3.45—nearly double the prior consensus of $2.43. CEO cited Wi-Fi 7 unit volumes surging 7x and Networks-for-AI orders raised to $2B+ for FY2026. This was HPE's first triple play since 2021. Demand strength expected to persist through fiscal 2027 and beyond, driven by DRAM/NAND-induced server pricing and AI infrastructure pull-through.

bullets.title: QQQ worst day of the year; Tech sector down 7.5% week; markets reprice Fed hike
bullets.body: After May payrolls surprised massively (172K vs. 88K est.), the QQQ fell 3.5% for its worst single day of 2026, with the Tech sector (XLK) off 7.5% from Tuesday's highs. NASDAQ 100 futures extended losses to 1.5% at their session low. Options flow turned bearish: QQQ saw $4.8B in delta outflows—double the worst 30-day precedent. Fed rate hike odds rose sharply to 63% by December (from 48%), and BNP Paribas forecast three hikes starting in December 2026. 2-year Treasury yields spiked to 4.147%.

bullets.title: Strong May jobs report (172K vs. 88K est.) reshapes Fed expectations
bullets.body: The May NFP print of 172K beat consensus of 88K by 4 standard deviations, and prior months were revised up 93K combined. Unemployment held at 4.3%. The data pushed Fed rate hike pricing to 63% by December and moved BNP Paribas to forecast three hikes starting in December. Cleveland Fed's Hammack subsequently warned that if trends continue, 'action could be necessary soon.' Goldman noted the market is 'overextended on growth hopes,' flagging H2 consumer health as the key swing factor.

bullets.title: Jensen Huang's Korea visit: R&D center, meetings with Samsung, SK Hynix, Hyundai; HBM4 qualified from all three suppliers
bullets.body: Nvidia's CEO visited Seoul post-Computex, meeting the chairmen of SK Hynix, Samsung, and SK Group. Nvidia confirmed HBM4 qualification from all three major memory suppliers (MU, Samsung, SK Hynix). Jensen also announced plans for an Nvidia R&D center in Korea and called robotics 'Korea's next key industry.' SK Hynix separately announced plans to double DRAM wafer capacity within five years, and SK Group Chairman said AI memory shortages could persist through 2030.

bullets.title: TSMC FY2026 revenue guide >30% and 2030 visibility unprecedented for foundry
bullets.body: TSMC Chairman CC Wei said the company still expects full-year revenue growth above 30%, adding that customer demand visibility extends to 2030—far beyond the typical few quarters. Wei noted that AI demand 'surprised everyone, even Nvidia CEO Jensen,' and that TSMC is avoiding aggressive price hikes. High-NA EUV is in research only; CoPoS advanced packaging pilot line established with meaningful volume expected in 2-3 years. TSMC Arizona Phase 1 1Q26 net profit alone exceeded all of CY25.

bullets.title: IREN closes $3.65B investment-grade GPU financing with Microsoft; announces 800MW Australia datacenter
bullets.body: IREN secured a $3.65B investment-grade GPU financing facility tied to its AI Cloud contract with Microsoft—described as the first facility of this kind. IREN also announced plans to build an 800MW data center campus in Bundey, South Australia, its first Australian project. Director insider buying of $35.1M at HOOD was noted; NBIS also disclosed a €8B investment in French AI cloud infrastructure endorsed by Macron.

bullets.title: Intel 18A gains momentum: Google qualifies EMIB-T, Marvell wins networking chip contract
bullets.body: Intel's 18A packaging (EMIB-T) is gaining customer traction, with Google qualifying it for the TPUv8t (Zebrafish) chip and Marvell reportedly winning a Google networking chip manufactured on Intel's 18A/18AP process with mass production targeted for end-2027. The EMIB-T adoption is partly driven by CoWoS capacity scarcity at TSMC. Applied Materials' Centura Sculpta EUV tool confirmed in use at Intel 18A. Intel closed strategic collaboration with Foxconn for next-gen AI infrastructure.

bullets.title: Retail investor sentiment at 5+ year bullish extreme; put/call ratio at 0.58
bullets.body: Options traders hit the most bullish sentiment in 5+ years with the put/call ratio falling to 0.58—a level associated with near-term fragility. Goldman's 1-Delta desk highlighted that the market is 'very long calls, not long downside hedges,' warning of a potentially violent transition if macro surprises emerge. The CBOE DSPX dispersion index hit its 3rd highest reading ever, signaling extreme single-stock vs. index volatility divergence.

bullets.title: AAOI surges 20%; optical sector gains traction on CPO/pluggable momentum
bullets.body: Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI) surged ~20% during the digest window, with multiple traders identifying it as the top US optical long ahead of a projected CPO/pluggables inflection in H2 2026. LITE hit all-time highs above $450, and COHR reached ATH on confirmation of an upgraded fab in Sherman, TX. Wiwynn's Computex booth displayed a CPO AI Accelerator using AyarLabs TeraPHY optical engines, with Lumentum supplying optics—validating supply chain roles. Jensen's NVDA invested $2B each into COHR and LITE in March.

bullets.title: NOK (Nokia) bullish thesis gains traction; Northland raises price target to $20
bullets.body: Northland analyst Tim Savageux raised his price target on Nokia to $20, calling NOK one of the best photonic plays with prior successful calls on MRVL and SIVE. Multiple traders cited NOK as a participant in EU CHIPS Act 2.0 and as a confirmed supplier in Nvidia's NVLink ecosystem via silicon photonics. A separate report noted NOK partnership with an XFAB silicon photonics play.

bullets.title: NBIS (Nebius) up 50%+ YTD; closes €8B France AI infrastructure deal
bullets.body: Nebius stock surged to record highs with market cap above $60B (+212% YTD), driven by: the €8B French AI cloud infrastructure deal announced with Macron, its NVDA Exemplar status, and a $471M take-or-pay agreement with Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab. Author who initially wrote the thesis noted NBIS outperforming the entire neocloud basket. A $2.7M put sweep was noted as a bearish outlier signal.

bullets.title: Tesla JPMorgan upgrade to Neutral ($475 PT); Tesla-SpaceX merger odds at 80%+
bullets.body: JPMorgan upgraded TSLA from Underweight to Neutral, raising its price target from $145 to $475 citing autonomous driving, robotics, AI, and software value. Wedbush maintained an 80%+ probability of a Tesla-SpaceX merger in 2027 post-SpaceX IPO. TSLA UK May registrations rose 18% YoY. The stock fell 4.6% on the day SpaceX's amended S-1 suggested potential equity issuance to acquire Tesla, with institutional investors citing conglomerate discount concerns.

bullets.title: HOOD Director Malka buys $35M+ in shares; Robinhood closes WonderFi Canada acquisition
bullets.body: Robinhood Director Meyer Malka purchased $35.1M in HOOD shares over the prior week through Bullfrog Capital—the first insider buy in one year and a potentially significant bullish signal. Separately, Robinhood closed its acquisition of WonderFi, entering the Canadian market. Trader @isamillionaire's subscriber community reported entering HOOD from $75.87.

bullets.title: Goldman raises S&P 500 year-end target to 8,000; tech concentration hits 39.7% of index
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs raised its 2026 S&P 500 year-end target to 8,000. The tech sector weighting in the S&P 500 hit a record 39.7%, up nearly 5 percentage points above the historical average—and nearly 5pp above the March 2000 dot-com peak. The S&P 500 posted 8-9 consecutive daily and weekly gains before reversing on the jobs report, with 23 all-time highs recorded in 2026.

bullets.title: WSTS revises 2026 semiconductor market forecast to $1.51T (+90%), memory +250%
bullets.body: The World Semiconductor Trade Statistics body dramatically revised its 2026 global semiconductor market forecast to $1.51T from $975B previously—a +90% jump—driven largely by memory (+250% to $800B+) and AI compute. Americas +112%, Asia Pacific +87%, Europe +58%. The 2027 market is projected at $1.9T (+27%). This aligns with SK Hynix's plan to double wafer capacity and Kioxia seeking long-term NAND supply agreements through 2029+.
